page: Google Cloud Platform c4n-standard-48-lssd is an x86_64 architecture server instance belonging to the c4n family. It is configured with 48 dedicated vCPUs and 180.0 GB of system memory, which translates to a resource density of 3.75 GB of RAM per core. The instance does not include GPU accelerators, and its local storage size is designated as none in the primary specifications, despite the local SSD reference in its name. It also does not include complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Due to the dedicated allocation of its 48 vCPUs, this instance provides predictable compute performance without the resource contention typical of shared-core environments. While benchmark data is currently unavailable for this specific configuration, the hardware profile represents a balanced resource distribution. From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the c4n-standard-48-lssd offers a high-density compute and memory allocation suitable for enterprise workloads that require stable, dedicated CPU performance without the premium cost of specialized memory-optimized or GPU-accelerated hardware.

The balanced vCPU-to-RAM ratio of approximately 1:3.75 makes this server type appropriate for a variety of general-purpose and compute-intensive workloads. Suitable use cases include medium-to-large database deployments, web serving at scale, application servers, containerized microservices, and CI/CD pipeline orchestration. The lack of GPU acceleration and local storage limits its applicability for direct deep learning training or high-IOPS local database caching, directing its optimal use toward CPU-bound distributed applications.
